conceptZh: 海是又大又廣、裝滿水的地方
object: a boxy toy robot built from mismatched parts and a dolphin
morph: the robot builds a wrong pond shape first, shrugs, and rearranges it into 海
creativeAngle: 玩具機器人先拼出小水坑，發現不對，一拉變成大海和海豚。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 海 (sea). Lead: a boxy gray toy robot with a long left arm and a short right arm. Moment 2 (1.7-3.4s): shrug, long-armed sweep and the blue pieces rearrange; on the second 海 the glyph is done, small waves clapping at its feet. Moment 3 (3.4-5.3s): a smiling gray dolphin jumps over the glyph in an arc; the voice says 海豚 as the robot ducks, spray drips on his short arm and he squeaks. Moment 4 (5.3-8s): glyph still; robot and dolphin balance a beach ball, bobbing slowly. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "海、海、海豚" (ㄏㄞˇ、ㄏㄞˇ、ㄏㄞˇ ㄊㄨㄣˊ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops; no other speech, no music louder than the voice. No vocabulary text, subtitles, watermark, clutter, flashing, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading.

conceptZh: 迴力賽車想衝去撞那個小小的藍水桶，卻衝過頭一頭撞倒第一塊藍色骨牌，骨牌一塊接一塊越倒越快排成「海」字，最後一塊把賽車彈飛栽進水桶，小水桶竟然倒出一大片大海。
object: a row of standing deep-blue domino tiles on pale sand, a squeaky pull-back toy race car with googly eyes, and one tiny blue toy bucket
morph: the car overshoots and nose-bonks the first tile; three small tiles topple left and lie down as the three water dots 氵, then taller tiles fall faster and faster into the right half 每, the last tile springboards the car into the bucket, which tips and gushes out an impossibly big sea below the finished glyph
creativeAngle: 改用骨牌連鎖的實體笨拙笑料取代上一版靜態海豚跳躍：賽車的「衝過頭」缺點直接引爆骨牌倒成海字，而詞語改用發音最安全的「大海」，並用「小水桶倒出超大的海」這個因果反差讓語音與畫面同時出現，完全不同於前一版的機器人與海豚。
promptEn:
An 8-second animated clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 海 (sea). Flat, bright toy-diorama look on a pale sandy cream floor, soft daylight, nothing busy behind.

Lead: a squeaky red pull-back toy race car with huge googly eyes and a tiny spoiler, the kind that always overshoots and crashes nose first. Across the frame stands a neat row of flat deep-ocean-blue domino tiles, small ones on the left, taller ones on the right. At the far right sits a tiny blue toy bucket half full of water, the car's goal.

Moment 1 (0–1.5s): the car at left locks its googly eyes on the bucket, revs backward with a rubbery squeak, wheels winding up, body squashing low. The voice says the first 海 as it launches forward in a blur.

Moment 2 (1.5–3.2s): it wildly overshoots its own braking point and BONKS nose first into the first blue tile with a cartoon squash, eyes spinning. The chain begins: three small tiles tip and flop leftward one after another, landing flat as the three water dots 氵 of the left side. Then the taller tiles fall faster and faster, clack clack clack, each knocking the next, dropping and settling into the right half 每: the short slanted top stroke, the horizontal, then the 母 body with its crossing stroke and two inner dots. The voice says the second 海 as the last tile claps into place and the correctly formed glyph lies complete.

Moment 3 (3.2–5s): the very last tile is a springboard; it whips up and flips the dazed car spinning end over end high across the frame, above the glyph, and it plops nose first into the little bucket at bottom right. A frozen beat. Then the bucket tips over and gushes out an impossibly big blue sea, far too much water for a tiny bucket, rolling as one soft wave along the bottom margin beneath the glyph. The voice says 大海 exactly as this big wave swells up and spreads.

Moment 4 (5–8s): the glyph stays perfectly still and readable while the car bobs upside down on the gentle waves at bottom right, rights itself with a wobble, and pops one front wheel up like a surprised thumbs-up, googly eyes rolling with a goofy grin. It never touches the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly 海、海、大海 (ㄏㄞˇ、ㄏㄞˇ、ㄉㄚˋ ㄏㄞˇ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, Taiwan standard readings, then stops. No other speech, no subtitles, only soft squeaks, clacks and a splash, and no music louder than the voice.

The only on-screen text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 海, formed from the fallen solid deep-ocean-blue tiles against the pale sandy cream background, correctly structured, centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins, held perfectly still for the final 3 seconds. No vocabulary text, watermark, clutter, flashing effects, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading.
